Alan Shearer.text: He joined his hometown club Newcastle United in 1996 for a then world record £15 million.
Alan Shearer.evidence: In the summer of 1996, he joined his hometown club Newcastle United for a then world record £15 million, and in his first season won his third consecutive Premier League Golden Boot.

Harry Kane.text: In 2023 he became the most expensive signing in Bundesliga history, joining Bayern Munich for €110 million.
Harry Kane.evidence: In 2023, Kane became the most expensive signing in Bundesliga history as he joined Bayern Munich in a transfer worth €110 million.

Wayne Rooney.text: He debuted for England aged 17 and is still the country's youngest-ever goalscorer.
Wayne Rooney.evidence: Rooney made his senior international debut for England in February 2003, aged 17, and is England's youngest-ever goalscorer.

Mohamed Salah.text: In his first Liverpool season he scored 32 league goals, a record for a 38-game Premier League season.
Mohamed Salah.evidence: In his first season, he set the record for most Premier League goals scored (32) in a 38-game season and helped Liverpool to the 2018 Champions League final.

Andy Cole.text: He was the first player to top both the Premier League's scoring and assist charts in the same season.
Andy Cole.evidence: He is the fifth-highest goalscorer in Premier League history with 187 goals, and used to hold the Premier League records for most goals scored in a 42-game season (34), the fastest player to score 50 goals (65 matches), and the first player to top both the Premier League's goalscoring and assist charts in the same season (1993–94).

Sergio Agüero.text: Debuting at 15 years and 35 days, he broke the Argentine league age record of his future father-in-law, Maradona.
Sergio Agüero.evidence: Agüero began his career at the Argentine club Independiente where, on 5 July 2003, he became the youngest player to play in the Argentine Primera División at 15 years and 35 days, breaking the 27 year record previously set by future father-in-law Diego Maradona.

Frank Lampard.text: He is one of the few footballers to have made over 1,000 competitive appearances.
Frank Lampard.evidence: He is also one of the few footballers to have made over 1,000 competitive appearances.

Thierry Henry.text: At Arsenal he won the Premier League Golden Boot a record four times.
Thierry Henry.evidence: Generally viewed as Arsenal's best ever player, he won the Premier League Golden Boot a record four times, three FA Cups and two Premier League titles, most notably as a cornerstone of the unbeaten Invincible season, after achieving a historic 24 goals and 20 assists the season prior.

Robbie Fowler.text: The Kop at Anfield nicknamed him "God", though he grew up an Everton fan.
Robbie Fowler.evidence: Renowned as a natural finisher who was predominantly left-footed, he scored 183 goals in total for Liverpool, and was especially prolific in his first three full seasons when he scored over 30 goals in each of them, earning the nickname "God" from the Kop at Anfield and twice being named PFA Young Player of the Year (1995 and 1996). ... As a youngster he supported Everton and regularly attended home and away games.

Jermain Defoe.text: He holds the Premier League record for most goals scored as a substitute, with 24.
Jermain Defoe.evidence: Defoe also holds the Premier League record for the most goals scored as a substitute, with 24.
